summary: Sets out the charter and rules for the general IETF discussion mailing list, including what topics belong there and what behavior is not acceptable, such as advertising. It is a Best Current Practice. It was replaced by RFC 9245.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3005 sets a charter for the general IETF discussion list. It describes the list's purpose, which topics belong there, and how repeated abusive posting may be handled.

subtitle: The charter for the IETF's general discussion mailing list.

tldr.problem: The broad IETF discussion list needed a charter describing its purpose and acceptable topics.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3005 defines the list's scope, examples of appropriate and inappropriate posts, and who may restrict posting in a pattern of abuse.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3005 was updated by RFC 8717 and later obsoleted by RFC 9245.

today: RFC 3005 is obsoleted by RFC 9245 and was updated by RFC 8717. The current charter is in RFC 9245.

sections.title: Purpose of the Discussion List
sections.content:
The IETF discussion list at ietf@ietf.org serves two purposes: discussing technical issues that further Internet technology, and discussing IETF direction, policy, meetings, and procedures. It is the most general IETF list, so it allows considerable latitude.

The list is for initial discussion. If a topic belongs to a working group or established list, discussion should move there when that is pointed out, unless wider input or direction is needed.
sections.plainLanguage: The list is a general place to begin discussions about Internet technology and IETF work. Topics with a more suitable forum should move there when possible.

sections.title: Appropriate and Inappropriate Posts
sections.content:
Appropriate postings include Last Call discussion of proposed protocol actions, technical issues that may become IETF work but lack an email forum, administrative policy, meeting questions, and announcements sponsored or endorsed by the Internet Society or IETF.

Inappropriate postings include unsolicited bulk email, unrelated subjects, unprofessional commentary, advertising, personal discussions, and announcements of events not sponsored or endorsed by the Internet Society or IETF.
sections.plainLanguage: Technical and administrative IETF topics belong on the list. Bulk email, advertising, personal discussions, and unrelated subjects do not.

sections.title: Restricting Abusive Posting
sections.content:
The IETF Chair, Executive Director, or a sergeant-at-arms appointed by the Chair may restrict posting by a person or a thread when inappropriate content represents a pattern of abuse.

They are encouraged to consider a person's overall posting pattern and whether a post is typical or an aberration. Complaints about decisions should be referred to the IAB.
sections.plainLanguage: Named IETF officials may restrict a person or thread when inappropriate content forms a pattern of abuse. Complaints about those decisions go to the IAB.
